transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Ariana (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Eli (CTO), Sana (Head ML), Marco (SRE), Olivia (Product)

[00:00] Ariana: Okay, good afternoon everyone. Thanks for carving out the time. Quick goal for today — lock down the POC success criteria for latency and throughput so our bench runs produce actionable numbers. We'll cover TTFT vs TPOT definitions, target percentiles, traffic mixes, and the measurement plan.

[00:22] Eli: Sounds good. We're mainly trying to validate that we can serve patient-facing summarization use cases with p99 latency under 350ms for short prompts, and maintain 200 rps for peak windows. So those are our rough anchors.

[00:41] Marcus: Got it. A couple of clarifying things — when you say p99 under 350ms, do you mean time-to-first-token (TTFT) or time-per-output-token aggregated (TPOT)? They imply different infra arrangements.

[01:05] Sana: We mean the user-visible latency. Practically, TTFT is most important for UX. But downstream token throughput matters for batch summarizations where we stream longer outputs. So we care about both, honestly.

[01:28] Priya: Just to align definitions — for this POC we recommend measuring: TTFT (time between request reaching service and first token emitted) measured at p95/p99, and TPOT as average per-token latency plus p95 for tail behavior. We'll show both.

[01:48] Marco: Quick note on env — our workloads have variable prompt lengths. Olivia will share examples but expect a bimodal distribution: ~60% one-paragraph short prompts, 35% medium essays (~400 tokens), 5% long diagnostics (~1200 tokens). Bursty traffic during morning syncs.

[02:10] Ariana: Perfect. That helps with sizing. For the POC measurement plan we typically run three passes: baseline cold start, warm steady-state with KV/prefix cache enabled, and sustained high-QPS stress-run to observe degradation/fallbacks.

[02:30] Eli: How do you simulate the streaming clients? We do web socket streaming in prod.

[02:38] Marcus: We have a harness that reproduces streaming behavior using wrk + custom stream client. For TPOT we do token-emit pacing; for TTFT we capture when the first byte hits the client. We also instrument Prometheus traces and capture flamegraphs for decoding hotspots.

[03:02] Sana: Do you use wrk or vegeta? We've had mixed results; vegeta handles percentiles better for us.

[03:10] Marcus: We can provide both configs. wrk for microsecond-level pushes, vegeta for sustained QPS and p95/p99 extraction. We'll also hand over a small JMeter script for the UI team if they prefer.

[03:29] Olivia: On success criteria — aside from latency/throughput numbers we also need stability: no more than 1% error rate at target throughput, and memory/GPU OOMs must be zero.

[03:44] Priya: Agreed. We typically include failure-rate SLOs: error% < 1% at nominal load, graceful degradation beyond that with fallbacks to smaller model. We'll record model-fallback events.

[03:58] Ariana: Let's propose concrete targets today so we're not vague: For short prompts (<= 60 tokens): TTFT p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms. For medium prompts (200-500 tokens): TTFT p95 <= 260ms, p99 <= 500ms. TPOT (per-token) targets: p95 <= 6ms, p99 <= 20ms. Peak sustained throughput target: 200 rps at 95% success. How does that land?

[04:33] Eli: Short prompts p99 350ms is okay, p95 180ms is aggressive but reasonable. For medium prompts the p99 500ms we can accept if throughput stays good. Will want to see the raw lat distribution though.

[04:50] Marco: One operational question — are your numbers with continuous batching and KV cache enabled? Those optimizations change TPOT a lot.

[04:59] Marcus: We'll run both cache-off and cache-on. Important to emulate your prefix reuse — if you frequently reuse the same patient preamble we should see large gains. We'll include a pass with simulated prefix cache hit rates of 0%, 30%, 60%.

[05:21] Sana: Great. Also want to understand warmup behavior: how many minutes/requests until KV/decoder caches fully populate?

[05:30] Priya: We'll capture warmup curves and report a steady-state window. For warmup we'll use synthetic traffic that ramps over 10 minutes, record metrics every 30s.

[05:44] Olivia: On measurement tooling — what counts as the canonical measurement for SLO pass/fail?

[05:50] Marcus: We'll define canonical runs as: 30-minute steady-state run at target QPS with your real prompt mix, collect p50/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT, error rate, and GPU util. If p99 targets are met for the short/med classes and error <1% we mark pass. We'll also provide time-series and raw samples for audit.

[06:12] Eli: What about network variability? Our prod is multi-region; we might have 30-40ms RTT. Will you run the tests from our VPC or from Redwood's hosted region?

[06:25] Ariana: Two options: (1) Redwood runs hosted harness in the same cloud region as your workload to approximate region RTT, or (2) we run harness inside your VPC via temporary agent for most accurate numbers. For the POC we recommend option 2 if you can allow an ephemeral testing VM.

[06:43] Marco: We can do an ephemeral agent in our VPC. We'll need instructions for required egress and IAM.

[06:49] Marcus: We'll send an agent playbook. It needs outbound to our benchmark collector and minimal ports for SSH. No inbound from outside except operators.

[07:05] Sana: On model variants — are you testing quantized variants? We do care about cost/latency tradeoffs.

[07:12] Priya: Yes, we'll test float32 baseline and 8-bit quantized variants where available. We'll include CPU fallback and a smaller family model that can be a fallback during overload. We'll measure quality delta with a small accuracy harness in parallel (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or custom task-specific metrics).

[07:35] Olivia: For the accuracy check, we want an eval set of 200 examples from our real anonymized transcripts. Is that sufficient?

[07:43] Sana: 200 is fine for spot checks; we will also run a longer eval post-POC.

[07:50] Marcus: Great. We'll include qualitative diffs and an MRR-style ranking for reranks if you use that pattern.

[08:00] Ariana: Timeline recap — Marcus will push the harness by 2025-08-22, Sana provides prompts by 2025-08-21, Marco sets up the ephemeral agent by 2025-08-23, Redwood runs baseline sweep and reports back by 2025-08-27, follow-up meeting week of 2025-08-29 to decide Dedicated vs Hosted.

[08:21] Eli: On billing during POC — we expect a limited free trial but may accept a small committed usage number for Dedicated evaluation.

[08:30] Ariana: We'll follow our standard POC terms; I'll include the POC billing note in the follow-up email.

[08:36] Olivia: Any open risks we should call out?

[08:40] Priya: Key risks: network egress bottleneck, insufficient prefix reuse (low cache hit), and unexpected model memory spikes with long contexts. We'll measure and highlight these.

[08:51] Marco: We'll also validate encryption/KMS for tokens; if you need HSM, we'll flag it early.

[08:57] Sana: One last question — how do you compute TPOT p99? Per-token across all requests or per-request aggregated?

[09:04] Marcus: We'll compute both. Primary TPOT p99 will be per-token across the corpus (this shows decoding tail), and we'll also produce per-request average token latency to surface worst requests. We'll annotate metrics with prompt class.

[09:20] Ariana: Okay, wrapping — I'll send the summary and attach the benchmark harness repo link and the agent playbook. Thanks everyone.

[09:29] Eli: Thanks. Looking forward to the numbers.

[09:33] (meeting ends)

Auto-generated summary (partial):
- Purpose: define pass/fail SLOs for Redwood POC focusing on TTFT/TPOT and throughput.
- Concrete SLOs proposed: short prompts TTFT p95 <= 180ms / p99 <= 350ms; medium TTFT p95 <= 260ms / p99 <= 500ms; TPOT p95 <= 6ms / p99 <= 20ms; sustained 200 rps at 95% success.
- Measurement plan: 3 passes (cold, warm with KV/prefix cache at several hit rates, and sustained stress), canonical 30-min steady-state run, harness using wrk/vegeta/stream client, instrumentation via Prometheus/traces/flamegraphs.
- Next steps and owners in action_items.
